title: "Execute the Pipeline"
subtitle: "Keep rendering and scientific execution separate"
execute:
  eval: false
engine: markdown

The historical branch uses the hand-delivered May 2025 ZIP exclusively and dynamically branches the approved W3
CSV preparation and legacy clinic-month inventory work. Page 16 tracks that
ZIP and extracts only its selected W3 and reviewed mapping sources; the
Google Drive/rclone mirror is excluded from historical inputs and comparisons. Branching is declared
here rather than in the transformation notebooks: each notebook defines
one-file transformation logic, while this graph defines dependencies and the
scheduler can distribute independent branches. Clinic-month branches track one
Parquet file per monthly member of the staged ZIP. Page 20 combines their paths
into a single Parquet inventory before collecting the reduced identity table.
Page 21 constructs the cross-wave diagnosis dictionary from the prepared
Wave 3 schema and archived source dictionaries and translations. Page 22
cleans and maps diagnosis measurements, selects report sources, and branches
over dictionary output groups. S4 currently uses the existing serial runner;
Slurm and controller configuration are outside this implementation.
Page 23 reconciles the frozen sectorization and reviewed spatial corrections,
constructs clinic healthsheds, and retains ordinary `sf` handoffs for pages
24–25. A cheap always-check target records the spatial package/native engine
versions and s2 setting; changed values invalidate the spatial read.
Page 24 assembles frozen coordinate sources, tests row-aligned intersections,
and retains candidates and the selected source for page 25.
Page 25 combines reporting history, reviewed spatial attributes, coordinate
selection, and neighbor evidence into two tracked metadata Parquet products.

Pages 26–28 implement the separate 2025–2026 source survey, cleaning, and
geospatial/final-aggregation work. Those deliveries are outside the old-wave
ZIP. These pages are now included by `tar_tangle()` here. The graph includes both
approved deliveries, final-product validation, internal candidate packaging,
and independent resource verification. Declaring or rendering this graph does
not execute it. Stagecoach owns the inputs; tracked R values in the notebooks
own transformation and release parameters. No separate preparation step is needed.

::: {.callout-note title="Track Data At Each Target Boundary"}

The current graph executes each per-file maximum in DuckDB and writes the
result to a branch-specific Parquet file. `targets` stores those file paths
rather than attempting to serialize live duckplyr relations. Page 18 declares
the final cross-file aggregation and cleaned Parquet output, included through
`tar_tangle()`. In-memory tables remain ordinary data targets; source files
and derived Parquet paths use `format = "file"` so their contents are tracked.

For dynamic file inputs, keep the path selector separate from file tracking.
`s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_paths_chr` returns the selected path vector as an ordinary
target. `s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_csv` then tracks one file per branch, and the
Parquet reducer branches over those tracked files. A static file target would
treat the whole vector as one bundle and cannot serve as that branch dimension.
This is the [documented file-branching pattern](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/dynamic.html#branching-over-files).

:::

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm The Execution Boundary"}

The runtime image and frozen R package library must exist. Approved inputs must
be staged under `data/inputs`. Run scientific target builds only inside the
compute-node allocation. Rendering and static/synthetic checks do not build targets.

:::

## Parallel targets execution plan

::: {.manual-procedure title="Plan One Allocation With Local Target Workers"}

**Planned configuration, not enabled by this page yet.** Legacy stage 4B is
absorbed into the existing runner and targets execution boundary. Submit one
Slurm allocation through the page-15 launcher and run one `tar_make()` manager
inside the project container. The manager will dispatch ready targets to local
R worker processes within that allocation.

The planned backend is the supported
[`crew` local controller](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/crew.html), selected
through `tar_option_set(controller = ...)`. The ordinary `tar_make()` call
remains the execution entry point; it has no new worker-count argument.
Do not port stage 4A's `future::plan(multicore)`, `future_map()` pools, or
`future.globals.maxSize` overrides into individual targets. Do not submit one
Slurm job for each diagnosis partition or use a Slurm worker-launcher plugin
for this single-allocation plan.

Illustrative configuration for a future reviewed resource profile:

```r
# Planning example only: not part of the emitted _targets.R below.
# Declare and lock crew through page 14 before enabling this configuration.
tar_option_set(
  controller = crew::crew_controller_local(workers = 2L)
)
```

Two workers are an example, not an established memory-safe default. Select the
worker count from measured branch requirements and the approved allocation.
The local controller creates separate R processes on the manager's node;
additional allocated nodes do not automatically become workers.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Plan Branch Memory, Threads, And Scheduling"}

Keep measurement-heavy operations inside bounded stage-4 targets and pass
Parquet paths between them. Schedule independent monthly, complete-period,
and output-group branches in parallel. Keep ordered spatial correction
rounds and other dependent transformations in their scientific sequence.

Before activation, record a versioned resource profile with:

| Resource | Required decision and verification |
| --- | --- |
| Allocation | One manager task, approved CPUs, total memory, wall time, and shared writable project/scratch storage |
| Worker concurrency | Explicit count within CPU and measured memory budgets, including manager overhead and retry behavior |
| Engine threads | Explicit per-worker DuckDB/BLAS thread budgets; do not give every worker the whole allocation's CPU count |
| Memory | Branch peak R plus engine memory, manager memory, and headroom; engine settings alone are not evidence of total process memory |
| Files | Branch-unique outputs, private temporary extraction/scratch, and read-only shared inputs |
| Environment | Same container, project working directory, and locked R library in every worker; initialize connections inside each process |

Use a representative month and output group as the first pilot. If a branch
does not fit its budget, reduce its working set or partition it at a safe
scientific boundary before increasing concurrency. Parallel execution does
not divide the memory required by one oversized target. Do not request a
blanket high-memory stage-4 job to compensate for collecting all waves in R.

Add `crew` to the direct dependency declaration and lock it only when the
controller implementation is introduced. The current `_targets.R`, runner,
and dependency lock remain unchanged by this detailed plan. The target graph
shown below is the currently implemented graph; pages 18–30 and internal candidate packaging are now wired into it.

:::

::::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-script-sh file="{{ emit.project_root }}/scripts/run-pipeline.R" mode="0755" title="Emit The Pipeline Entry Point"}

```r
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

script_arg <- grep("^--file=", commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE), value = TRUE)
script_path <- if (length(script_arg)) sub("^--file=", "", script_arg[[1]]) else ""
if (!nzchar(script_path)) {
  stop("Could not determine the pipeline runner path.")
}

repository_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path(dirname(script_path), ".."),
  mustWork = TRUE
)
setwd(repository_root)
targets::tar_make()
```

::: {.manual-procedure title="Execute The Declared Graph"}

Run the graph explicitly after reviewing the target declarations. This builds
the scientific products; rendering the preceding code only emits the runner
and graph.

After changing the release declarations, render this page to re-emit
`_targets.R` before the next authorized pipeline run. Packaging creates
`data/outputs/releases/v0.1.0/` for the initial page-19 version, including its
resources, verification files, and `datapackage.json`.

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run scripts/run-pipeline.R
```

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Verify The Initial Graph"}

When the parallel controller is implemented, add synthetic execution tests
that establish serial/parallel result equality, correct per-file branching,
observed worker concurrency, allocation-compliant thread/memory use, worker
environment consistency, and no extra Slurm submissions. After an authorized
pilot, retain its peak-memory/timing evidence and confirm a no-op second run.
Those future resource checks have not run during this planning work.

Check file tracking and every dynamic branch dimension without building the
pipeline. In particular, a file target used as a branch dimension must itself
have a pattern; an ordinary path-vector target may serve as the first dimension.

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript tests/check-data-storage-convention.R
```

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript -e \
  'stopifnot(all(c("s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr", "s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_csv", "s0_clinic_RMA_W3_within_file_max_parquet", "s2_clinic_months_deduplicated_parquet", "s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet") %in% targets::tar_manifest()$name))'
```

The declaration check above can run before a build. After execution, confirm
that no target reports an error and that the graph is current; neither command
builds the targets again.

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript -e \
  'errors <- targets::tar_meta(fields = error)$error
   stopifnot(!any(!is.na(errors) & nzchar(errors)), length(targets::tar_outdated()) == 0L)'
```
